records.reason: A compact ketone anchor at 20/1 tests whether broad predicted carbonyl tails transfer to a simple scaffold, complementing measured delayed carbonyl rows 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 and f90a5a5a54509c085ebd.
A fluorinated ketone at 50/1 samples a higher-solvent carbonyl condition and tests endpoint-tail transfer from the measured delayed carbonyl regime in 0c5c35afb3a24375c153.
This aromatic ester at 20/1 adds an independent completion-tail probe for comparison with broad measured ester behavior and helps separate ester effects from carbonyl-only corrections.
A simple nitrile aromatic at 5/1 provides an acceptor-rich anchor against the severe basic-aromatic failures in 49201b5817f204116f7f and a17bcdddcf0799baeee2.

A cyano acetophenone combines two acceptors without basic nitrogen, testing whether delayed behavior extends beyond the pyridyl and amine-containing failures represented by 49201b5817f204116f7f and 4659b6752f23c0b85f08.

A brominated heteroaromatic provides a compact-side heteroatom control for the basic and acceptor-rich region, where measured rows 062e85da36395276eb89 and cfcf2b8c54d4c8b3838a were less uniformly delayed.
The low-strength m72 condition probes the compact side of the strong m72 response, complementing measured delayed m72 rows 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 8e7636d7a60a6058305a.
A benzophenone at 1/1 and higher loading supplies a compact carbonyl condition anchor for comparison with the severe completion tails in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153.
A heavy aromatic at 10/1 tests whether high solvent strength alone creates a completion tail in a nonpolar scaffold, constraining corrections learned from polar failures.
A second nonpolar heavy-atom aromatic at 20/1 provides a condition-diverse compact reference for distinguishing genuine tails from broad prediction intervals.
A simple fluoro ketone under PE conditions provides a mobile-phase contrast to DCM carbonyl rows and tests whether endpoint movement is condition-specific.
A chloroiodobenzene at 2/1 is a compact heavy-atom control for the predicted broad intervals in halogenated aromatics, reducing risk of global tail inflation.
A nonpolar alkene at 2/1 in PE broadens compact hydrophobic coverage and tests whether completion corrections learned from carbonyls transfer to hydrocarbons.
A hydrophobic ester at zero EA probes whether ester completion broadening begins under weak solvent, complementing the delayed ester and carbonyl examples in H_TAIL.
A phenoxyethyl acrylate at 1/1 provides an intermediate ester condition for learning whether solvent changes shift onset and completion together.
An indene-like compact aromatic under PE provides a nonpolar baseline against which broad predicted intervals for heteroatom-rich rows can be calibrated.
A highly loaded diiodoaromatic probes loading effects in a nonpolar scaffold, testing whether loading-driven tails are structural or general.
A fluoro-iodotoluene at 10/1 adds a heavy-atom condition contrast and a compact control for high-solvent aromatic predictions.
This m187 aldehyde condition creates a loading contrast with measured m187 behavior in 7707be94729b49b3a560 and tests whether aldehyde completion changes independently of onset.
A brominated aromatic ether at high PE strength probes completion-tail transfer into a donor-free, acceptor-poor scaffold, complementing measured aldehyde and ester tails.
A hydrophobic aldehyde at 5/1 tests recurrence of aldehyde completion tails outside strongly polar families, using measured delayed aldehyde behavior in 8f625c2f36dcacfc8ed5 as context.
An ester at 1/1 in PE provides a moderate compact-side ester reference for comparison with the broader predicted ester regime.
A halogenated aldehyde at 1/1 and higher loading tests whether aldehyde completion broadening is sensitive to loading, complementing the endpoint-specific evidence from f90a5a5a54509c085ebd.
A donor-containing iodoaromatic at high loading probes whether donor and heavy-atom effects combine into a delayed tail, extending the scaffold-specific donor evidence from 48853fd78c77153b963a.
A methoxy naphthalene ester at 5/1 provides fused aromatic ester coverage and tests whether aromatic fusion widens V2 independently of V1.
A brominated alkylbenzene in PE supplies a compact hydrophobic loading and solvent reference for distinguishing structural heavy-atom effects from tail corrections.
The second m187 condition forms a local aldehyde response contrast with 872cc42767a008d75dc6 and measured 7707be94729b49b3a560, testing ratio sensitivity.
A long-chain aryl ketone at 1/1 tests whether hydrophobic carbonyls remain compact or develop broad completion under ordinary conditions.
The second m49 condition forms an aldehyde response contrast across ratio and loading, helping calibrate the hydrophobic aldehyde region near measured a6d05356a06b44affa38.
A dimethoxy aldehyde at 2/1 tests whether additional ether acceptors widen completion relative to simpler aldehydes, supporting transferable functional-group learning.
A difluorobenzaldehyde at 10/1 supplies a structurally simple aldehyde condition probe for separating solvent-driven completion tails from substitution-specific effects.
A heavy aromatic ester at 2/1 and high loading tests combined ester, halogen, and loading effects while providing a bridge between compact ester rows and broad completion regimes.

hypotheses.content: V2 errors cluster in broad, delayed-completion regimes across carbonyl, ester, aldehyde, and donor-containing families, while structurally nearby rows can remain compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Independent tail labels can teach endpoint-specific V2 corrections without globally widening compact rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected carbonyl, ester, and aldehyde probes retain broad completion after condition matching?

hypotheses.content: Solvent strength, loading amount, and loading-solvent volume interact locally and can produce abrupt V1/V2 transitions rather than one smooth global loading effect.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched condition contrasts provide local response-surface information and reduce extrapolation between compact and delayed regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed scaffold, does changing ratio or loading shift onset and completion together, or primarily change V2?

hypotheses.content: Basic or acceptor-rich aromatic structures form a transferable but condition-sensitive failure region, with nitrile, pyridyl, fused heteroaromatic, and multi-carbonyl examples differing strongly in magnitude.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs interaction features beyond generic aromaticity, HBA count, or polarity to identify delayed basic-aromatic rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can simple nitrile and heteroatom controls distinguish functional-group effects from the severe basic-aromatic regime?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic structures show scaffold-specific and endpoint-specific retention tails; donor count alone does not determine the response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Donor-family contrasts can separate ring attachment, flexibility, and loading from a generic HBD correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor scaffold and condition combinations identify compact versus delayed elution?

hypotheses.content: V1 and V2 can respond differently to condition changes, with completion tails appearing or widening while onset remains comparatively stable.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separate endpoint calibration can reduce V2 error without damaging the better-calibrated V1 surface.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched aldehyde and ester conditions change V2 more than V1?

hypotheses.content: Compact measured rows inside broad predicted regimes are needed to prevent failure repair from becoming global tail inflation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Compact anchors constrain endpoint calibration and help distinguish genuine local failures from ordinary prediction spread.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which simple hydrophobic and heteroaromatic conditions remain compact despite broad model intervals?

feedback_interpretation: Recent labels strengthened the local-interaction interpretation. The m177 series shows that loading can change V2 dramatically with little onset movement. Donor results in 48853fd78c77153b963a and compact references such as 5910d3761883c7036a58 weaken a donor-count-only rule. The large m159, m141, m146, and m211 errors support a condition-sensitive basic and acceptor-rich failure region, while simpler controls are less uniformly delayed.
batch_rationale: The batch uses condition contrasts across carbonyl, ester, aldehyde, donor, and acceptor-rich families, alongside compact heavy-atom and hydrocarbon controls. Repeated m187, m49, and related functional-group conditions test local response curves; independent aldehyde, ester, and carbonyl probes repair V2-tail failures across the Row-distribution. Compact controls constrain overcorrection and help the retrained QGeoGNN learn where delayed completion is structural, condition-dependent, or absent.
